metadata.coaching_cue: Advance position before submission: Escapes -> Guard -> Pass -> Side Control -> Mount -> Back.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Stephan Kesting's BJJ Roadmap organizes grappling into six interconnected major positions: Closed Guard, Open Guard, Half Guard, Side Control, Mount, and Rear Mount (Back Control). Top players advance from guard passing to pins and submissions; bottom players protect frames, recover guard, and sweep to top before hunting finishes.
title: BJJ Roadmap: The 6 Core Positions and Positional Hierarchy

metadata.coaching_cue: Pull knees toward your chest while stripping sleeve grips before climbing a high collar grip.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: From Closed Guard bottom, use both legs together to bring the top player's hips forward while breaking their biceps or lapel grips. Once their posture collapses below 45 degrees, anchor one hand deep in the collar or behind the neck to set up sweeps and submissions.
title: OSJJ Closed Guard: Breaking Posture with Collar Tie and Hip Pull

metadata.coaching_cue: Escape your hips out to the side, lay your top shin across their belt line, and pull them onto your shin before scissoring.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Secure a cross-collar grip and same-side sleeve grip in Closed Guard. Shrimp onto your side, place the top shin diagonally across the opponent's torso and the bottom leg flat on the mat blocking their knee, load their weight forward, and scissor cleanly into full Mount.
title: BJJ Roadmap Closed Guard: Classic Scissor Sweep and Hip-Out Angle

metadata.coaching_cue: When your opponent postures upright, open guard, post on your far hand, drive hips high into their chest, and trap their posting arm.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Against an upright top player in Closed Guard, sit up onto your elbow and then palm, drive your hips explosively across their centerline to block their post and sweep to Mount. If they post a hand wide on the mat, immediately switch to the Kimura figure-four or Guillotine choke.
title: BJJ Roadmap Closed Guard: Hip Bump Sweep to Kimura and Guillotine Chain

metadata.coaching_cue: Feed the first hand thumb-deep behind the neck, keep wrists straight, and flare elbows back toward your ribs instead of pushing.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Break posture first so the first palm-up grip reaches the back tag of the collar. Feed the second grip either palm-up underneath or palm-down over the shoulder, pull the opponent's chest down with your knees, and squeeze wrists straight across both carotid arteries.
title: OSJJ Closed Guard: Deep Cross-Collar Choke Mechanics

metadata.coaching_cue: Control one arm across centerline; if they pull the trapped arm out, shoot hips high for the Triangle and cut a 90-degree angle.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Isolate one arm across your torso with a high guard climb. Pivot perpendicular to throw the leg over the face for the straight armbar; if they stack or yank the arm free while leaving one arm in and one arm out, lock the Triangle behind the knee and angle off toward the trapped shoulder.
title: BJJ Roadmap Closed Guard: Armbar and Triangle Choke Dilemma

metadata.coaching_cue: Stay on your side with a diagonal knee shield, block the crossface first, then pummel a deep hip underhook to come up into dogfight.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Never lie flat on your back in Half Guard. Maintain a diagonal top knee shield and top hand collar frame to deny the crossface. Shoot the bottom arm underneath their far armpit to grab their far hip or thigh, hide your head low on their chest, and build base to sweep or take the back.
title: OSJJ Half Guard: Knee Shield Frame to Underhook Dogfight Sweep

metadata.coaching_cue: Pass the trapped foot to your outside hand, block their posting foot, and drive forward into their far hip.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Once you win the underhook in Half Guard, reach underneath their trapped knee to capture the toes of their trapped foot. Drive forward across their base; if they whizzer hard and lean back into you, tuck your head and roll underneath into the Plan-B sweep.
title: BJJ Roadmap Half Guard: Old School Sweep and Plan-B Roll-Through

metadata.coaching_cue: Build two rigid frames on their neck and near hip, bridge to create space, shrimp your hips away, and insert the bottom knee.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Keep both elbows glued to your ribs under Side Control so the top player cannot isolate an arm. Wedge your top forearm across their throat and bottom forearm into their hip crease, bridge to lighten their chest pressure, hip escape outward, and thread your bottom knee through to recover guard.
title: BJJ Roadmap Side Control Escape: Neck-Hip Frames and Shrimp to Guard

metadata.coaching_cue: When they block your knee recovery by driving toward your hips, swim your top arm inside for a deep underhook and turn onto your knees.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: If the top player switches hips or crowds your lower body to stop the classic shrimp, bridge toward them to open space beneath their far armpit. Pummel your top arm through for a tight underhook, tuck your chin, and turn to your knees into a low single-leg finish or turtle stand-up.
title: OSJJ Side Control Escape: Far-Side Underhook to Knees or Single Leg

metadata.coaching_cue: Turn their chin away with shoulder pressure before attacking the far elbow with an Americana or stepping over for a Kimura.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Stabilize Side Control for the full 3 seconds with a deep crossface and far hip block. When the bottom player pushes on your chest, pin their wrist to the mat with a monkey grip for the Americana keylock, or transition to North-South Kimura if they straighten the arm.
title: BJJ Roadmap Side Control Top: Crossface Pin to Americana and Kimura

metadata.coaching_cue: Trap one arm and the same-side ankle tightly, then bridge explosively over your shoulder rather than straight up.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: When mounted, keep elbows tight and wait for the top player to post a hand or reach for your collar. Clamp that arm to your chest, hook the same-side foot with your heel so they cannot base out, and bridge diagonally over your shoulder to land inside their Closed Guard.
title: BJJ Roadmap Mount Escape: Trap and Roll (Upa) Bridge Escape

metadata.coaching_cue: Flatten one leg to the mat, frame on their hip and knee, shrimp onto your side, and scoop their ankle into Half Guard.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Pair the Elbow-Knee escape with the Trap-and-Roll. Turn onto your side while keeping your bottom leg flat on the mat, wedge your elbow inside their knee, bridge slightly, and slide your bottom knee underneath their leg to capture Half Guard and then recover Closed Guard.
title: OSJJ Mount Escape: Elbow-Knee Escape to Half Guard and Full Guard

metadata.coaching_cue: Walk your knees into their armpits as soon as their elbows lift off the mat to shut down bridges and open the S-mount armbar.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: After securing 4 points in Mount, grapevine or widen your base to absorb the initial bridge. Threaten the cross-collar choke to force their hands upward, walk your knees high under their armpits, transition to S-mount, and finish the mounted armbar with tight knees.
title: BJJ Roadmap Mount Top: Climbing to High Mount for Cross Choke and Armbar

metadata.coaching_cue: Keep chest glued to their upper back, fall to the underhook side to trap their bottom arm, and align your elbow directly under their chin.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Lock both hooks inside the thighs without crossing your ankles to earn 4 points. Maintain a tight seatbelt grip with the choking arm over the shoulder, fight two-on-one to clear their defensive hands, and finish the Rear Naked Choke or bow-and-arrow collar choke.
title: BJJ Roadmap Back Control: Seatbelt Grip, Over-Under Side, and Rear Naked Choke

metadata.coaching_cue: Control the choking wrist with both hands first, peel the bottom hook, and slide your shoulders flat to the mat on the underhook side.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Survival comes before escaping hooks. Immediately tuck your chin and grip the choking wrist two-on-one. Shift toward the non-choking (underhook) side, clear the bottom leg hook, drive the back of your head and shoulders to the mat, and turn into their top Half Guard.
title: OSJJ Back Escape: Two-on-One Hand Fight and Back-of-Head to the Mat

metadata.coaching_cue: Seal your elbows to your knees so hooks cannot enter, control their near wrist, and either sit out or roll through to guard.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Never stay static in bottom Turtle where opponents can insert hooks for 4 points or lock a clock choke. Keep elbows glued to thighs, defend the collar grip with two hands, and use a far-shoulder Granby roll or sit-out turn-in to recover Closed or Half Guard.
title: OSJJ Turtle Bottom: Protecting Collar Space, Sit-Out, and Granby Guard Recovery

metadata.coaching_cue: Insert your near knee behind their hip, lock the seatbelt grip, sit to your hip behind them, and pull them across your lap for both hooks.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Attacking Turtle begins with chest-to-back weight and a deep seatbelt harness. Instead of forcing hooks from straight behind, wedge your bottom knee into their hip pocket, sit to your side (chair sit), pull them onto your bottom hook, and insert the top hook cleanly.
title: BJJ Roadmap Turtle Top: Seatbelt Entry and Chair-Sit Back Take

metadata.coaching_cue: Sit forward with head lower than theirs, clamp their posting arm, fall onto your ear rather than your back, and elevate with the top hook.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Keep active seated posture in Butterfly Guard with both insteps hooked inside the thighs. Win an underhook or overhook to kill their posting arm on one side, drop your shoulder toward the mat at a 45-degree angle, and lift with your top butterfly hook directly into Mount or Side Control.
title: BJJ Roadmap Butterfly Guard: Underhook Hook Sweep and Shoulder Crunch

metadata.coaching_cue: Keep at least three points of contact (grips and feet on hips/biceps) and square your hips continuously whenever they circle.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Open Guard succeeds through constant tension between hands and feet. Maintain collar-sleeve or De La Riva frames so the passer cannot control both pant cuffs simultaneously, and use hip movement plus shin-to-shin frames to off-balance them before they clear your knee line.
title: OSJJ Open Guard: Three-to-Four Points of Contact and Angle Retention

metadata.coaching_cue: Pin their knees to the mat before stepping around on Toreando, or win the far underhook before sliding your shin across for Knee Cut.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Effective guard passing alternates outside speed passes (Toreando) with inside pressure passes (Knee Cut and Over-Under). Control the feet and hips first, clear the knee line past their frames, and settle chest-to-chest for 3 full seconds to score 3 points.
title: BJJ Roadmap Guard Passing: Toreando Bullfighter and Knee Cut Pass

metadata.coaching_cue: Pin the trapped leg to your chest with head pressure in their far hip, tripod to clear the foot, and switch hips into Side Control.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: The Over-Under pass neutralizes flexible open guards by immobilizing one leg on the mat while wedging your shoulder into the opponent's lower abdomen. Keep your head glued to the far hip to prevent triangles, step over the bottom shin, and establish heavy Side Control.
title: OSJJ Guard Passing: Over-Under Pressure Pass and Hip Switch

metadata.coaching_cue: Win inside collar control, circle to make them step heavy onto the lead foot, and snap their head down as you scoop the ankle.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: For Jiu-Jitsu competition, low-risk Gi takedowns minimize guillotine exposure. Snap the opponent's posture down with a deep collar grip; as their weight loads onto the forward heel, drop your level cleanly to block the ankle or whip them past your hip with a Collar Drag for 2 points.
title: BJJ Roadmap Takedowns: Low-Risk Collar Drag and Cross-Collar Ankle Pick

metadata.coaching_cue: Keep your ear glued to their chest and posture tall on the Single Leg; on defense, shoot hips heavy to the mat and crossface.
metadata.license_note: MIT-licensed RollMetrics coaching cues paired with public YouTube instructional timestamp jump-links (Stephan Kesting / GrappleArts, Lachlan Giles / Absolute MMA, Jon Thomas).

text: Shoot with a proper level change rather than bending at the waist, keeping your head tightly pressed inside their torso so they cannot lock a Guillotine. Finish by running the pipe or sweeping the far ankle, and always defend opponent shots by sprawling hips heavy onto their shoulders.
title: OSJJ Takedowns: Head-Inside Single Leg Finish and Fundamental Sprawl Defense
